hens_rule_text: up to 6 hens per lot, only with a chicken permit from the Norfolk Department of Public Health
permit_notes: Permit from the Norfolk Department of Public Health, Bureau of Environmental Health, must be approved before getting chickens. Search summaries report a one-time fee of about $50 and leg or wing ID bands on each hen. A permit is void where private restrictions ban chickens.
setback_notes: Search summaries of the permit rules report coops at least 15 ft from any property line and 20 ft from a neighbor's dwelling; not confirmed from full code text.
coop_rules: Hens kept in a coop and enclosure meeting permit standards; feed in rodent-proof containers.
zoning_notes: Reported to apply to single-family detached lots.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: Norfolk Department of Public Health chicken permit application (Virginia Department of Health)
BackYard Chickens: Norfolk Virginia chicken ordinance

research_notes: Facts come from search-result extracts of the official health department permit application and quotes of City Code 6.1-7; the PDF and Municode timed out or were blocked, so the full text was not read. Setback figures and the fee come partly from secondary summaries.
